key_insight: Kinematically consistent mappings connect nonlinear isogeometric beams to fluid interfaces while preserving work-conjugate motion and load transfer.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables slender structures in partitioned fluid–structure interaction to use reduced-dimensional beam models under large deformations.
method: Attach fluid-interface points to the beam in the reference configuration.
Reconstruct interface motion using nonlinear Bernoulli or Timoshenko beam kinematics.
Linearize the mapping consistently and use its transpose for work-conjugate load transfer.
evidence_signal: Analytical deformation tests, convergence studies, virtual-work checks, and beam-based Mok, Turek–Hron, and Goland wing flutter benchmarks support mapping accuracy and coupled-FSI applicability.
watch_item: Implementation must account for configuration-dependent mappings and the distinct cross-sectional rotation descriptions of the two beam formulations.
paper_title: Consistent Mapping for Fluid Structure Interaction with Geometrically Nonlinear Isogeometric Beams
